column1: instrumental§She was instrumental in getting the archive digitized and appears nowhere in the acknowledgements.§她在推动档案数字化上**起了关键作用**，致谢里却不见她的名字。§instru（装备，同 instrument 工具）
insubstantial§The evidence is insubstantial and the conclusion is confident, which is the combination reviewers most distrust.§证据**单薄**而结论笃定，这是审稿人最不信任的组合。§in-（不）+ substance（实质）
insufferable§He is insufferable about the one prediction he got right and silent about the eleven he did not.§他为唯一说中的那次预测**得意得让人受不了**，对没说中的十一次则闭口不谈。§in-（不）+ suffer（忍受）
insufficient§Two hours' notice is insufficient for a decision that will bind the council for the next nine years.§对一个将约束议会未来九年的决定来说，两小时的通知**远远不够**。§
insular§The department became insular after 1990, and its papers stopped citing anything published elsewhere.§这个系在 1990 年后变得**封闭孤立**，其论文不再引用别处发表的任何东西。§insul（岛，同 island 岛屿）
insurgent§The insurgent faction won four seats and, within a year, controlled the entire committee.§这个**反叛的**派系赢下四个席位，一年内就控制了整个委员会。§in-（进入）+ surg（升起，同 surge 涌起）
insurrection§The insurrection lasted nine days and changed a law that four decades of petitions had not.§这场**起义**持续九天，改变了四十年请愿都没能改变的一条法律。§in-（进入）+ surrect（起立，同 resurrect 复活）
integral§The stairwell is integral to the structure, which is why removing it would take the whole east wall with it.§这道楼梯间是结构**不可或缺的**部分，所以拆掉它会带塌整面东墙。§integ（完整，同 integrity 完整）
intelligible§The explanation became intelligible only after she drew it, and the drawing took about forty seconds.§这个解释直到她画出来才变得**可理解**，而画图用了大约四十秒。§inter（在中间）+ leg（选择／读，同 legible 易读的）
intemperance§His intemperance in argument cost him allies who agreed with almost everything he said.§他在争论中的**不知节制**让他失去了几乎处处同意他的盟友。§in-（不）+ temper（调和，同 temperate 温和的）
intemperate§The intemperate email was deleted within an hour and had already been screenshotted by four separate recipients.§这封**言辞过激的**邮件一小时内被删，却早已被四位收件人分别截了图。§
intentional§The omission was intentional and defensible, and the report explains neither of those things.§这处遗漏是**有意的**且说得过去，而报告对这两点都没有解释。§intent（意图）
intercede§A retired judge interceded on his behalf, and the sentence was reduced from nine years to four.§一位退休法官为他**说情**，刑期从九年减到四年。§inter（在中间）+ ced（走，同 recede 后退）→ 走到中间去
intercept§Coastguards intercepted the boat nine miles out, and everyone aboard was ashore before midnight.§海岸警卫队在九英里外**拦截**了这条船，船上所有人午夜前都上了岸。§inter（在中间）+ cept（拿，同 capture 捕获）
interleave§The editor interleaved the letters with the diary entries, and the two together tell a story neither tells alone.§编者把书信与日记条目**交错编排**，两者合起来讲出了各自都讲不出的故事。§inter（在中间）+ leave ← leaf（书页）
interlocutor§Her interlocutor for nine years was a man she never met, and the letters run to four volumes.§九年里她的**对话者**是一个她从未谋面的人，往来书信有四卷之多。§inter（在中间）+ locut（说，同 eloquent 雄辩的）
interloper§The committee treated her as an interloper for two years and elected her chair in the third.§委员会把她当**闯入者**看待了两年，第三年选她做了主席。§inter（在中间）+ lope（跑）
interminable§The meeting was interminable and decided nothing, and the same item appeared on the next agenda.§这场会议**没完没了**却什么也没决定，同一项议题出现在了下次的议程上。§in-（不）+ termin（终点，同 terminal 终端）
intermittent§The fault is intermittent, which is why four engineers have inspected the machine and found nothing.§这个故障是**间歇性的**，所以四位工程师检查过这台机器却什么也没发现。§inter（在中间）+ mitt（送，同 transmit 传送）→ 中间断一下
interrogation§The interrogation ran nineteen hours, and the confession it produced was thrown out on appeal.§这场**审讯**进行了十九小时，由此得到的供词在上诉时被排除。§inter（在中间）+ rog（询问，同 rogation 请求）
intonation§Her intonation gave the answer away: the words were neutral and the pitch was not.§她的**语调**泄了底——用词是中性的，音高不是。§in-（进入）+ ton（声调，同 tone 音调）
intractable§The problem is intractable rather than hard: every solution creates a worse problem somewhere else.§这个问题是**棘手难解的**而非困难的——每个解法都在别处制造一个更糟的问题。§in-（不）+ tract（拉，同 tractor 拖拉机）→ 拉不动
intransigence§Her intransigence on one clause held up an agreement that both sides badly wanted.§她在一条条款上的**不肯让步**，卡住了一份双方都急切想要的协议。§in-（不）+ transig（达成）
intransigent§The most intransigent negotiator in the room was also the only one without authority to concede anything.§屋里最**寸步不让的**谈判者，也是唯一没有让步权限的那个。§
intrepid§The intrepid surveyor mapped nine hundred miles of coast in a boat built for a river.§这位**无畏的**测量员用一条为河道建造的小船测绘了九百英里海岸。§in-（不）+ trepid（惊惧，同 trepidation 恐惧）
intricate§The mechanism is intricate and robust: forty moving parts, and it has run since 1911 without a rebuild.§这个机构**精细**而耐用——四十个活动部件，自 1911 年运转至今未曾大修。§in-（进入）+ tric（麻烦，同 extricate 解脱）→ 缠成一团
intrigue§The proposal intrigued the committee enough that they asked for a second presentation the same week.§这份提案让委员会**很感兴趣**，他们同一周就要求再讲一次。§in-（进入）+ tric（麻烦）→ 把人绕进去
introspection§Nine months of introspection produced one useful sentence, which she now teaches on the first day.§九个月的**内省**产出了一句有用的话，她如今在第一天课上就讲它。§intro（向内）+ spect（看，同 inspect 检查）
intrude§He would not intrude on a grief he did not share, and he wrote instead, four weeks later.§他不愿**打扰**一份自己并不共有的悲痛，于是四周后写了封信。§in-（进入）+ trud（推，同 protrude 突出）
intruder§The intruder took nothing and moved nine objects, which is what frightened the family most.§这名**闯入者**什么也没拿，却挪动了九件东西，这是最让那家人害怕的。§
intrusive§The questions were intrusive rather than difficult, and four of the six people simply stopped answering.§这些问题是**侵扰性的**而非困难的，六个人里有四个干脆不再回答。§
intuition§Her intuition about the sample was right, and it took two years of work to show why.§她关于这个样本的**直觉**是对的，而花了两年工作才说明为什么。§in-（进入）+ tuit（看，同 tutor 导师）→ 一眼看进去
intuitive§The interface is intuitive for people who already know the task and baffling for everyone else.§这个界面对已经懂这项任务的人来说是**符合直觉的**，对其余人则令人困惑。§
inundate§The office was inundated with four thousand applications for nine posts, and reading them took the whole summer.§办公室被四千份申请**淹没**，而职位只有九个，读完它们花了整个夏天。§in-（进入）+ und（波浪，同 abundant 丰富的）
invalidate§A single missing signature invalidated nine hundred ballots, and the recount changed the result.§一个缺失的签名让九百张选票**作废**，重新计票改变了结果。§in-（不）+ valid（有效的）
invariable§His answer is invariable: he asks what problem the change is meant to solve, and usually nobody knows.§他的回答**一成不变**——他问这个改动要解决什么问题，而通常没人知道。§in-（不）+ vari（变化，同 vary 变化）
invasive§The invasive species arrived in ballast water and now outnumbers every native fish in the lake.§这个**入侵**物种随压舱水而来，如今数量超过湖中任何一种本地鱼。§in-（进入）+ vas（走，同 evade 逃避）
inverse§The relationship is inverse and strong: the more inspectors a district has, the fewer violations it records.§这种关系是**反向的**且很强——一个辖区检查员越多，记录的违规就越少。§in-（不）+ vers（转，同 reverse 倒转）
investigation§The investigation took four years and reached the conclusion the first officer had written in week one.§这项**调查**花了四年，得出的结论正是第一位警官在第一周写下的。§
invigorate§A change of route invigorated a class that had walked the same four miles every week for a term.§换一条路线**振奋**了一个整学期每周走同样四英里的班级。§in-（进入）+ vigor（活力，同 vigorous 精力充沛的）
inviolable§The confidentiality of the ballot is inviolable, which is why the recount had to be done in public.§选票的保密性是**不可侵犯的**，所以重新计票必须公开进行。§in-（不）+ viol（侵犯，同 violate 违反）
invocation§The invocation of an emergency power that had not been used since 1948 alarmed even the government's allies.§援引一项自 1948 年起未曾动用的紧急权力，这一**援引**连政府的盟友也感到不安。§in-（进入）+ voc（呼唤，同 voice 声音）
invoke§Lawyers invoked a statute from 1892, and the court agreed that it had never actually been repealed.§律师**援引**了一部 1892 年的法令，法院同意它其实从未被废止。§
irascibility§His irascibility was famous and, colleagues agreed, entirely reserved for people who wasted other people's time.§他的**易怒**很出名，而同事们一致认为，它只留给那些浪费别人时间的人。§ira（愤怒，同 ire 怒火）
iridescent§The beetle's iridescent shell has no pigment at all: the colour comes entirely from the structure of its surface.§这种甲虫**虹彩闪烁的**外壳完全没有色素，颜色全部来自表面结构。§Iris（虹之女神）
ironic§It is ironic that the safety review was cancelled to save the money the accident later cost forty times over.§**讽刺的**是，安全评审为省钱而取消，而那场事故的代价是这笔钱的四十倍。§
irony§The irony was lost on the audience, and the speaker spent four minutes explaining that he had been joking.§这份**反讽**观众没听出来，演讲者花了四分钟解释自己是在开玩笑。§
irrational§The fear is irrational and the behaviour it produces is perfectly sensible given the fear.§这种恐惧是**非理性的**，而它所导致的行为，就恐惧本身而言完全合理。§ir-（不）+ ration（理性，同 reason 理由）
irrationality§The irrationality is systematic, which means it can be predicted and, in four documented cases, exploited.§这种**非理性**是有规律的，意味着它可以被预测，并在四个有据可查的案例中被利用。§
irrefutable§One irrefutable fact remains: the money left the account four hours before the meeting began.§有一个**无可反驳的**事实存在——钱在会议开始前四小时离开了账户。§ir-（不）+ refut（驳斥，同 refute 反驳）
irrelevant§Most of the file is irrelevant, and the four pages that matter were filed under the wrong year.§卷宗大部分是**不相干的**，而要紧的那四页归档时放错了年份。§ir-（不）+ relevant（相关的）
irrepressible§Her irrepressible enthusiasm carried the project through a year in which nothing at all went right.§她**抑制不住的**热情，带着项目熬过了一整年没有一件事顺利的时光。§ir-（不）+ repress（压制）
irreproachable§His conduct was irreproachable and his judgment was not, and only the second one mattered here.§他的品行**无可指摘**而判断力不然，而在这里只有后者要紧。§ir-（不）+ reproach（责备）
irresolute§The chair was irresolute for four meetings, and by the fifth the decision had been made elsewhere.§主席**优柔寡断**了四次会议，到第五次时决定已在别处做出。§ir-（不）+ resolute（坚决的）
irresponsible§Publishing the figure without the margin of error was irresponsible, and four newspapers repeated it.§不附误差范围就发布这个数字是**不负责任的**，而四家报纸转载了它。§
irreverence§Her irreverence toward the founders' portraits offended the trustees and delighted every student in the hall.§她对创始人肖像的**不恭**冒犯了理事们，却让礼堂里每个学生开心。§ir-（不）+ rever（敬畏，同 revere 尊敬）
irreverent§The irreverent tone of the guidebook is why it sells, and why the museum refuses to stock it.§这本导览**不敬无忌的**语气正是它畅销的原因，也是博物馆拒绝上架的原因。§
irritable§He becomes irritable after nine hours without food, and everyone who works with him has learned the schedule.§他九小时不进食就变得**易怒**，与他共事的人都记熟了他的时间表。§irrit（激怒）
irritate§The tone irritated people whom the substance would have persuaded, which is a mistake he makes often.§这种语气**惹恼**了那些本会被内容说服的人，这是他常犯的错误。§
isolation§Isolation, not the illness itself, is what four of the nine patients described as the hardest part.§九位病人中有四位描述最难的部分是**隔离**而非疾病本身。§insul（岛，同 island 岛屿）→ 孤岛化
iterate§They iterated the design nine times, and the version that shipped was closest to the second.§他们把设计**反复迭代**了九次，而最终出货的版本最接近第二版。§iter（再次）
itinerant§The itinerant teacher covered four villages a week and kept the only school records that survive.§这位**巡回的**教师每周跑四个村子，也保存下了唯一存世的学校记录。§itiner（旅程，同 itinerary 行程）
jade§Nine months of night shifts jaded a nurse who had arrived, four years earlier, genuinely eager.§九个月的夜班让一位四年前满怀热忱而来的护士**心生倦怠**。§
jeopardize§One unguarded sentence at the reception jeopardized a negotiation that had taken eleven months to arrange.§招待会上一句没把住门的话**危及**了一场筹备了十一个月的谈判。§
jingle§The jingle ran for forty years, and four generations can sing it without remembering the product.§这段**广告小调**播了四十年，四代人都会唱，却记不得是什么产品。§
jingoism§The jingoism of the period is embarrassing to read and was, at the time, almost universally popular.§那个时期的**沙文主义**读来令人难堪，而在当时几乎人人拥护。§源自一首好战歌曲里的 by jingo
jocular§His jocular manner in the ward was a discipline, not a temperament, and the patients relied on it.§他在病房里**诙谐的**做派是一种自律而非性情，病人们依赖着它。§joc（玩笑）
jubilant§The jubilant crowd stayed for hours, and the players had gone home before most of them left.§**欢腾的**人群待了好几个小时，球员们在多数人离场前就已回家。§jubil（欢呼）
